items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Recommendation: block security-sensitive releases and gated public exposure; conditionally allow ordinary reversible growth only when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Evidence: the security baseline reports no fleet-doctor run; operations reports no deploy, uptime, or error sweep results; security sitefacts are unknown across the managed fleet; and no evidence is available for authentication boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release integrity, dependency provenance, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, or security.txt/disclosure readiness. Compliance evidence confirms HTTPS for checked sites but does not establish complete TLS, access, release, or data controls. Risk severity: high for release and public-exposure decisions; medium for contained reversible growth. Exact decision: retain the current security gate, continue the existing read-only evidence matrix, and do not claim certification or a clean bill of health.

Retain the existing security evidence work only. Complete or attach authorized evidence for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release and deployment controls, TLS, dependency and supply-chain provenance, data exposure, monitoring and incident signals, and security.txt or disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.

For any go-live or security-sensitive implementation, require a completed security review before admission. Current status is needs_owner because material control evidence is absent. Reconsider only after dated evidence supports access control, secret handling, runtime isolation, release integrity, TLS, dependency provenance, data-flow protection, monitoring and incident response, disclosure readiness, and an owner-approved disposition.
